summary: Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago. He served on the faculty at Texas Christian University (attested 2001).

Don Handelman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at McGill University (~1958–1964), the University of Pittsburgh (~1964–1967), and the University of Manchester (~1967–1971). He was Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).
Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Wilhelm Geiger from circa 1894 to 1897.

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Bard College, the University of Pennsylvania, Oxford (~1980–1981), and Yale (~1977–1984). He joined the University of Pennsylvania's Department of Linguistics faculty around 1985.

Donald Capps was a religious studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark College (~1956–1960), Yale Divinity School (~1960–1963), and the University of Chicago (~1965–1970). He held posts at UNC Charlotte (~1974–1981) and Princeton Theological Seminary (~1981–2009).

Donald E. Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Stanford (~1970–1975) under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda. He served on the faculty at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2011).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and later served at Harvard University as Distinguished Visiting Professor of Buddhism (2004–2010) and Distinguished Visiting Fellow (~2004–2012).
Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Washington University in St. Louis (~1960–1964). He held a post at Emory University from circa 1982 to 2019.
Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle (attested 2005), and Ludo Rocher.

Donald S. Lopez Jr. works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1974–1982) under Jeffrey Hopkins. His posts include Middlebury College (~1983–1989) and the University of Michigan, where he was appointed in 1990.
Dor Bahadur Bista is a Tibetologist who studied at Tri Chandra College (~1950–1954). He served as a Professor at Tribhuvan University from circa 1985 to 1995.
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology and related fields. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorji Wangchuk is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his MA and doctorate at the University of Hamburg (~1994–2002) under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. He became a professor at the University of Hamburg around 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She is a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009).
Douglas Matthew Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016) under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.

Douglas Ober works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (~2011–2017) under Harjot Oberoi.

Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, earned an MA at the University of Washington (~1997–1999) and a PhD at SOAS (~2000–2004) under Ulrich Pagel. He was appointed Senior Lecturer at Massey University circa 2005.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~2000–2005) under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has taught at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University (~2007–2014).
